messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 Paging: Elevated 5xx + streaming disconnects observed across gateway-streaming-prod. Alert threshold triggered at 12:03:54 UTC (request error ratio > 6% over 5m). Investigate and escalate if customer impact.
maria: acked. I'm on call and looking. @sre-oncall do you want to take lead for mitigation? :mag:
sre-oncall: taking. brief summary: spike in 5xx and TIMEOUTs on streaming endpoints, increased client cancels. Affects both chunked and paged streaming flows. Looks like gateway -> fanout -> runtime path, errors originating around gateway timeouts and occasional chunk truncation.
devon: adding context — we're seeing a pattern where client CANCEL events spike immediately before connection closes, but the runtime logs show a few half-closed streams and 499-like disconnects from downstream. Could be proxying or keepalive regression.kevin: running quick checks on gateway metrics now. curl test against /v1/stream returns an open connection then abrupt RST after ~3s on some hosts.
kevin: curl output snippet:
```
$ curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" "https://gw.example.internal/v1/stream?model=gpt-mini"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
 ... some chunks ...
[partial chunk]
Connection reset by peer
```
liz: I see increased 504 from the edge LB to gateway in the last 5m — connections queuing up at gateway acceptors. Possible acceptor thread saturation or slow backend handoffs.
alice: customer-success flagged 3 customers reporting partial responses and reconnect loops. Severity is P2 for now, but could escalate if not contained.
sre-oncall: plan: 1) enable immediate degrade policy to fallback to non-streaming paged responses for high error routes 2) widen gateway timeouts slightly to reduce premature resets 3) roll a small canary to route traffic to older gateway pool with known-stable kernel settings 4) collect tracer and runtime stacks from failing traces.
maria: can we do 1 and 2 safely from console? I can roll the policy and change timeouts if someone confirms the UI knobs.
devon: yes — we have a runtime route policy named streaming-failover. Toggle will route STREAM requests to paged-fallback if errors > 5% for 2m. Toggle command (console):
```
POST /admin/routes/streaming-failover/toggle
{ "state": "on", "threshold": 0.05 }
```
maria: toggled streaming-failover ON at 12:08:15 UTC. Will monitor.
kevin: bumped gateway read timeout from 5s -> 10s at 12:09:02 UTC on pool-a. Applying to pool-b now.
liz: pool-b timeout bumped. Observing slight drop in 504s, but chunk truncation still present in a subset. Looks like a downstream process dropping mid-chunk.
kevin: pulled runtime logs for request id 2026f9c3:
```
[runtime] WARN incomplete-frame: chunk-length-mismatch for req=2026f9c3
[net] ERR write: broken pipe
[proxy] INFO client_cancelled true
```
alice: CS: impacted customers report that partial output appears then client immediately retries; some SDKs treat partial chunk as failure and close stream which compounds the problem.
devon: hypothesis: a combination of gateway short read buffer + edge TCP RSTs from keepalive timeout is causing the runtime to observe broken pipes mid-chunk. Also seeing a small uptick in TLS renegotiation counts on the LB.
sre-oncall: next steps executed: - toggled failover (done) - increased keepalive on LB from 60s -> 120s (in progress) - added temporary proxy bypass for a subset of traffic (route to gw-legacy pool) as a hotfix. gw-legacy receives ~10% of traffic now.
maria: gw-legacy routing in place at 12:14:40 UTC. Early customer reports show that one affected customer sees full streams again.
kevin: running live trace tool for a failing request: tracer shows long SND/ACK gap between gateway and runtime (~2.8s) before connection reset. Attaching trace ID: trace-3190001234-7
```
# tracing summary
span[gw]->span[fanout]->span[runtime]
fanout wait: 2800ms
```
liz: also noticed increased goroutine count on gateway acceptance loop prior to spike. Could be GC or epoll backlog. CPU was normal but syscalls for accept rose.
devon: can we temporarily reduce concurrent streams per connection to avoid head-of-line blocking? There's a knob on gateway: max-inflight-streams-per-conn. Recommend dropping from 50 -> 20.
sre-oncall: lowering max-inflight to 20 on pool-a at 12:18:10 UTC, pool-b scheduled in 2m.
maria: made the change for pool-b at 12:20:05 UTC. Monitoring RPS and error ratio.
kevin: error ratio decreased from 6.5% -> 2.4% over 10m after the combination of failover + timeout/keepalive tweaks + inflight reduction.
alice: CS confirming initial customers reporting restored behavior. Affected customers: acct-914, acct-221. They saw reconnects reduced and partial output resolved.
devon: still seeing occasional incomplete-frame logs but overall volume down. We'll keep the legacy pool as fallback for 30m then evaluate rollback.
liz: filing an action item for infra to reproduce under load — create a test that simulates many small-chunk streams with client-side abrupt cancels.

Action items:
- devon: reproduce in staging with chunk-heavy workload and client cancels (by EOD)  
- infra (liz): investigate gateway acceptor backlog and provide kernel/epoll metrics for last 24h (tomorrow)  
- runtime (kevin): add extra logging around chunk framing and add metrics for incomplete-frame events (PR queued)  
- maria: coordinate with CS to notify impacted customers and confirm resolution in 1h

sre-oncall: marking incident as mitigated at 12:28:55 UTC — moving to monitoring. Will escalate to P1 if error ratio rises above 5% again. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident annotated: mitigated_by = sre-oncall; mitigated_at = 12:28:55 UTC; ticket = INC-319000
maria: thanks everyone. Good job on the quick containment. We'll run a proper RCA tomorrow and decide if we need a config permanent change or code fix.
kevin: sharing quick grep for the incomplete-frame pattern to help RCA:
```
rg "incomplete-frame|chunk-length-mismatch" -n runtime/ | sed -n '1,120p'
```
devon: FYI I'll follow up in #eng-runtime with traces and a proposed fix to make chunk-writes atomic w.r.t. connection state.
alice: CS will send a short postmortem email to impacted accounts after the RCA.
